newsitem.title: USA: Ten injured in San Francisco hotel fire.
newsitem.headline: Ten injured in San Francisco hotel fire.

text.p: Ten people were injured and hundreds left homeless by a fierce fire that raced through a residential hotel in San Francisco, officials said Tuesday.

Fire department investigators said the fire, which broke out late Monday night at the Delta Hotel, was started by a cigarette left in a chair. They said the tenant responsible could face a reckless endangerment charge.

The top two floors of the five-story Delta Hotel, home to many elderly and poor people, were gutted in the blaze. The rest of the hotel and the neighbouring Baldwin House Hotel suffered smoke or water damage.
More than 120 firefighters were called out to the blaze and they used ladders to rescue some residents from upper floors.
Eight residents were taken to city hospitals suffering from smoke inhalation and two firefighters had minor injuries, San Francisco Fire Department spokesman Lt. Edward Campbell said.
Andrew Smith, a spokesman for the American Red Cross, estimated that up to 400 people had been evacuated from the Delta and the Baldwin House hotels.

The Red Cross set up a shelter in a recreation centre near the hotel and 220 people were registered there on Tuesday morning, Smith said. "We think the remainder of residents stayed with family or friends in the area," he said.

Smith said the shelter would remain open as long as needed and the American Red Cross was looking for more permanent housing for evacuees. The Red Cross would also give evacuees vouchers to buy clothes and groceries, he said.
